subject: Aligning Marketplace Price Floors, Accelerated Rebates, and Distributor Uplift for BrightLayer PO
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@brightlayer.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing detail request for private offer (BrightLayer)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightLayer is excited about the performance profile for the inference runtime. Procurement asked me to consolidate a few technical pricing questions before we move to the PO stage:

1) Marketplace price floor: our finance team requires a minimum list price floor for any private offer routed through the AWS Marketplace. Can you confirm whether Redwood can set a list-price floor on a private offer and how that interacts with reseller pass-through?

2) Accelerated rebate schedule: we have an internal program that prefers back-loaded discounts when committed usage hits 60/90/120 day milestones. Is Redwood able to structure an accelerated rebate (payable as a credit invoice) tied to usage cadence?

3) Distributor/reseller uplift: BrightLayer will work through a distributor in EMEA and wants to understand whether distributor uplift (a percentage over net) can be recognized in the PO and whether that uplift affects the marketplace list price or is handled separately as a reseller fee.

Please send an outline of possible structures and any operational constraints (billing flows, invoicing cadence, evidence required for rebates). We may need AWS Marketplace input as well — copied them here.

Attachments: BrightLayer_RFP_Q3.pdf (RFP excerpt).

Best,
Maya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, BrightLayer
procurement@brightlayer.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Procurement Team <procurement@brightlayer.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing detail request for private offer (BrightLayer)

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached a short worksheet to illustrate the two structures we typically run.

- List-price floor: Yes — we can set a private-offer list price that establishes a floor. On AWS/GCP/Azure private offers the list price is what appears on the marketplace record; discounts in the PO can’t reduce the public list price but the private offer defines the transaction price.

- Accelerated rebate: We can implement a rebate schedule as a crediting mechanism after usage milestones. Operationally that runs as a retrospective credit (invoice credit) tied to usage evidence; we need usage reports and a reconciliation window (30 days) to process.

- Distributor uplift: Two options: (A) pass-through reseller fee — the distributor invoices BrightLayer separately and we show net revenue; (B) include reseller uplift as an explicit line in the private offer (we can add a reseller-fee line item so it’s part of the PO economics). Option B requires an explicit contract clause and will affect revenue recognition flow across marketplaces.

I've attached redwood-proforma-worksheet-BL.xlsx with examples for (i) 'list-floor + credit rebate' and (ii) 'list-floor + reseller-fee line item'. Take a look and tell us which you prefer.

Next step: if BrightLayer prefers option (ii) we'll loop in legal and partner ops to confirm distributor invoicing path and tax handling.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Internal thinking:
- Proposed default: set marketplace list-price floor at $0.15/token equivalent (this is illustrative in the worksheet). Then offer accelerated rebate schedule: 5% @ 60d, 8% @ 90d, 12% @ 120d (credit applied to next invoice).
- Distributor uplift: prefer handling as a reseller-fee line item (so BrightLayer sees it in the PO and distributor receives separate settlement). Proposed uplift 7% of net usage (paid to distro). If we do pass-through, we need a clear mapping in the reporting so channel ops can process the distributor payment.
- Tax/Invoice: listing reseller-fee as a PO line will mean Redwood collects and passes through? Legal will need to confirm. If distributor invoices BrightLayer directly, Redwood doesn't handle the uplift financially (simpler).

Ask: Ben / Irene — can partner ops commit to supporting an explicit reseller-fee line in the private-offer flow and provide the settlement path (pay-to distributor account) if BrightLayer wants that in the PO? Kim — any concerns on MSFT/Azure taxonomy differences (we might have to map line items differently on each marketplace)?

If we agree, I'll send back a clean proposal to BrightLayer and loop AWS Marketplace to confirm legal/billing constraints.

Jonas

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightlayer.com, aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing detail request for private offer (BrightLayer) — ops question

Thanks for the summary, Jonas. Partner ops can support an explicit reseller-fee line in the private offer but with two guardrails:

1) We need the distributor legal entity and bank details at time of PO so we can create a pay-to mapping in our settlement system. Without that, we default to pass-through (distributor invoices BrightLayer).

2) For marketplace compliance, when a reseller-fee is included as a PO line we must not reduce the documented list price — the list price remains the same and the distributor fee is shown as an additional line. This is workable but requires a short addendum in the PO contract.

Operationally we recommend the following final approach for BrightLayer (we'll send a formal PDF):
- Private offer list-price floor: set at $0.15/token-eq on the marketplace record (establishes floor visibility).
- Accelerated rebate (crediting): 5% after 60 days usage threshold, 8% after 90 days, 12% after 120 days — credits applied to Redwood invoices following 30-day reconciliation and usage proof.
- Distributor uplift: include explicit reseller-fee line at 7% of net usage in the PO. Distributor bank/legal details to be provided by BrightLayer. If distributor details are not provided at PO time we will default to pass-through and document the difference.

Next steps: Jonas, please share the attached updated proforma (I've edited the worksheet with the final numbers). Maya — can you confirm which workflow you prefer and provide distributor entity details if you choose the reseller-fee-in-PO option?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Partner Revenue, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
